plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (MgF2/HfO2 chirped stack) based on iteration_06 results (best_target_score=0.647). Four complementary routes proposed: (1) Localized reinitialization per feedback directives - freeze layers 1-9, tighten bounds on layers 10-20; (2) Periodic photonic crystal topology from evidence with AR matching; (3) Extended layer count (26 layers) to test degrees-of-freedom scaling; (4) Alternative SiO2/SiNx material pair with same chirped topology. All routes maintain parent_route_id=route_02 per refinement_chain requirement.

routes.title: Localized reinitialization of MgF2/HfO2 chirped stack with frozen front section
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Freezing layers 1-9 at iteration_06 optimal values while applying ±3 nm perturbation bounds to layers 10-20 will reduce residual ripple artifacts in the 400-700 nm sub-band without degrading passband transmission, as the thinner rear layers dominate phase accumulation errors in the visible stopband.
routes.design_principle: Localized optimization with asymmetric bounds: coarse stopband shaping locked in front section, fine phase correction in rear section where non-quarter-wave deviations cause visible-band ripple.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 20 finite layers from the incident side: HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2
manufacturing_considerations: Sub-100 nm layers require precise thickness control
Ion-assisted deposition recommended for HfO2 density and moisture stability
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for coherent multilayer interference
Phase accumulation sensitivity scales with optical thickness; thinner layers exhibit higher relative phase error for fixed absolute thickness tolerance
expected_advantages: Reduced optimization search space improves convergence
Frozen front section preserves established stopband edge shaping
Tight bounds on rear layers target ripple sources identified in iteration_06 spectra
known_risks: Over-constraining may prevent global optimum discovery
Fixed front layers may lock in suboptimal phase relationships
routes.execution_request_english: Perform one bounded TMM thickness optimization for an exactly 20-layer planar stack. Use the fixed material sequence from the incident side: HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2. Optimize only the physical thickness of each finite layer within the user-declared bounds. Do not optimize material identity or layer count in this route. Optimize a 20-layer MgF2/HfO2 alternating stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layers 1-9 fixed at thicknesses: [144.99, 130.26, 125.53, 124.68, 126.05, 121.32, 116.58, 111.84, 97.11] nm. Layers 10-20 initialized at [95.67, 87.63, 84.42, 88.16, 83.42, 78.68, 63.95, 69.21, 54.47, 49.74, 55.00] nm with optimization bounds ±3 nm around these seeds. Material sequence: MgF2(layer1), HfO2(layer2), alternating. Optimize for maximum mean transmittance 255-280 nm, minimum mean transmittance 300-700 nm, minimum mean transmittance 700-1100 nm. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with coherent TMM solver. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Direct implementation of feedback directive: localized reinitialization with ±3 nm bounds on layers 10-20, layers 1-9 frozen at iteration_06 optimal values to target visible-band ripple artifacts.

routes.title: Periodic photonic crystal stack with AR matching from evidence
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic (L/2 H L/2)m photonic crystal structure with anti-reflection coatings, as demonstrated in CorpusId:199509322, will achieve sharper stopband edges and higher passband transmission than the chirped topology for the same layer count, due to constructive interference periodicity.
routes.design_principle: 1-D photonic crystal with periodic main-function units sandwiched between AR coatings; periodicity creates well-defined photonic bandgaps with predictable stopband centers.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 3 finite layers from the incident side: HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2
manufacturing_considerations: Periodic structure requires high thickness uniformity across all periods
AR coating thicknesses sensitive to substrate index matching
theory_basis: Photonic bandgap theory for 1-D periodic structures
Bragg condition for stopband center wavelength
AR coating theory for impedance matching
expected_advantages: Sharper stopband edges from periodic constructive interference
Predictable stopband center from layer thickness ratio
Evidence-backed design from successful solar-blind UV filter fabrication
known_risks: Periodic structure may have narrower stopband than chirped design
AR coatings add complexity and may introduce passband loss if mismatched
routes.execution_request_english: Perform one bounded TMM thickness optimization for an exactly 3-layer planar stack. Use the fixed material sequence from the incident side: HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2. Optimize only the physical thickness of each finite layer within the user-declared bounds. Do not optimize material identity or layer count in this route. Optimize a 22-layer MgF2/HfO2 periodic photonic crystal stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Structure: 3-layer AR coating | 8 periods of (MgF2/2, HfO2, MgF2/2) | 3-layer AR coating. Initialize AR layers at 25 nm, 40 nm, 25 nm; initialize periodic unit layers at 25.5 nm, 39.3 nm, 25.5 nm per evidence. All layers optimizable with bounds 10-150 nm. Material sequence alternates MgF2 and HfO2. Optimize for maximum mean transmittance 255-280 nm, minimum mean transmittance 300-700 nm, minimum mean transmittance 700-1100 nm. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with coherent TMM solver. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Topology change from chirped to periodic photonic crystal based on evidence CorpusId:199509322 demonstrating successful solar-blind UV filter with this architecture; tests whether periodicity outperforms chirped dispersion for dual-stopband requirement.

routes.title: Extended 26-layer MgF2/HfO2 chirped stack for increased degrees of freedom
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 20 to 26 while maintaining chirped topology will improve dual-stopband suppression (300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm) by providing additional phase correction degrees of freedom, with diminishing returns expected beyond 26 layers.
routes.design_principle: Layer count scaling: more interfaces provide finer spectral control at cost of manufacturing complexity; 26 layers remains under 30-layer constraint while adding 30% more degrees of freedom.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 26 finite layers from the incident side: HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2
manufacturing_considerations: Total optical thickness may exceed 3 µm requiring stress management
Ion-assisted deposition recommended for layer density
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method scaling with layer count
More interfaces enable finer spectral shaping at cost of cumulative absorption and scattering
expected_advantages: Improved stopband depth from additional reflection interfaces
Better separation of 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm suppression bands
Test layer-count scaling law for this specific bandwidth ratio
known_risks: Increased total thickness may cause stress-induced delamination
Diminishing returns beyond 20 layers may not justify manufacturing cost
Optimization convergence may slow with more variables

Use the fixed material sequence from the incident side: HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2 / HfO2 / MgF2. routes.revision_reason: Layer count increase from 20 to 26 tests whether additional degrees of freedom improve dual-stopband performance; maintains chirped topology from route_02 but expands design space.

routes.title: SiO2/SiNx material pair with chirped topology from evidence
routes.scientific_hypothesis: SiO2/SiNx material pair from CorpusId:199509322 will achieve comparable or better stopband suppression than MgF2/HfO2 due to higher refractive index contrast (SiNx ~2.0 vs HfO2 ~2.2, SiO2 ~1.46 vs MgF2 ~1.38), enabling fewer layers or deeper rejection for the same layer count.
routes.design_principle: Material pair substitution: maintain chirped topology from route_02 but replace MgF2/HfO2 with SiO2/SiNx to test index-contrast scaling of stopband depth.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 20 finite layers from the incident side: SiNx / SiO2 / SiNx / SiO2 / SiNx / SiO2 / SiNx / SiO2 / SiNx / SiO2 / SiNx / SiO2 / SiNx / SiO2 / SiNx / SiO2 / SiNx / SiO2 / SiNx / SiO2
manufacturing_considerations: SiNx requires NH3 nitrogen precursor for low extinction coefficient per evidence
SiO2/SiNx compatible with ALD for precise thickness control
Material absorption edges must be verified for 255 nm transparency
theory_basis: Fresnel reflection coefficient scales with index contrast delta-n
Higher contrast enables deeper stopbands with fewer periods
Material absorption must remain negligible at 255-280 nm passband
expected_advantages: Higher index contrast may enable deeper stopbands
SiNx ALD compatibility supports space-qualified deposition
Evidence-backed material pair from successful solar-blind UV filter
known_risks: SiNx may have higher absorption at 255 nm than MgF2
Material optical constants may differ from bulk values in thin-film form
Requires experimental n,k characterization for accurate TMM modeling

research_influence: CorpusId:199509322 evidence directly motivated route_02_periodic_pc (periodic photonic crystal topology) and route_02_sio2_sinx (SiO2/SiNx material pair), providing experimentally validated design principles for solar-blind UV filters
CorpusId:211025653 evidence on HfO2 IAD deposition stability informed manufacturing_considerations for MgF2/HfO2 routes, supporting space-platform environmental requirements
Feedback directive on localized reinitialization directly shaped route_02_refine_localized with frozen front layers and ±3 nm bounds on rear layers
unresolved_decisions: Optimal layer count between 20-30 layers for this dual-stopband requirement remains unknown; route_02_extended_layers tests 26 layers but 28-30 may offer further improvement
Material absorption at 255 nm for SiNx requires experimental verification; TMM solver will use registry values but thin-film deposition may alter optical constants
Incidence angle and polarization state not specified in original request; routes assume normal incidence and unpolarized light, but space platform may require angular robustness
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
